transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Michael (DataHarbor Head of ML), Sara (DataHarbor SWE), Tom (DataHarbor CTO)

Summary:
Quick scoping to align on benchmark goals, harness integration, streaming vs non-streaming behavior, success criteria, and timeline for a 2-week POC. Customer to provide traffic scripts; Redwood to provide harness adapter and run initial baseline on hosted + dedicated variants.

Topics:
- Success criteria and SLA targets
- Workload sizing and representative scripts
- Harness integration (customer scripts -> Redwood runner)
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs
- Pass/fail for bench and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm alex from Redwood inference, i'm the AE on this account. priya here is our sales engineer.
[00:04] Priya: hi all, yeah thanks. quick agenda, want to confirm success criteria, get sample workload shapes, and talk harness integration, streaming behavior and timelines.
[00:12] Michael: sounds good. on our side tom and sara are here. we want to validate latency under our peak load and also check cost tradeoffs. for us the two big things are 95th percentile latency under load and consistency of outputs, i.e. no regression in quality versus our current baseline.
[00:25] Tom: yep, and security is obviously important — SOC 2, SSO, and ability to deploy in our VPC later if things look good.
[00:33] Alex: totally, we'll send the SOC 2 pack and security appendix after this call.
[00:36] Sara: quick note — our current baseline is a mix of streaming for chat flows and non-streaming for batch summarization. so both patterns matter.
[00:45] Priya: okay good. can you share numbers for peak concurrency and qps? that'll help size the harness.
[00:50] Michael: rough numbers — production peaks at ~400 concurrent chat sessions, average of 1.8 requests per session per minute, spikes up to ~650 concurrent during our morning window. batch jobs are smaller in concurrency but heavy in token count — like 100 jobs running in parallel each generating 15k tokens.
[01:10] Priya: got it. for the POC we typically run two buckets: representative steady-state traffic to validate cost/latency and a short stress window to validate saturation and fallbacks. does 400 concurrent steady + a 10-minute spike to 650 sound right?
[01:20] Michael: yes that's our core SLO. for success criteria: 95th pct latency under 300ms for short chat responses (<= 64 tokens), and under 1.2s for longer streaming segments; batch throughput should average >10k tokens/sec aggregated across the cluster — roughly translate to our cost targets.
[01:38] Alex: good to capture that. i'll note success criteria as: 95th pct latency targets, cost per 1k tokens below the threshold you specified, and no functional regressions on our eval prompt set.
[01:47] Tom: one note — we want deterministic output quality. we run an eval suite, if rouge/bleu degrade by more than 2% we consider it a regression.
[01:55] Priya: that's helpful — please send the eval suite or a subset. for harness integration, do you currently have a load generator?
[02:00] Michael: yes we have a set of k6 scripts and some internal python runners that simulate sessions and streaming. we can share them.
[02:06] Priya: perfect. typical approach is: customer shares scripts + sample dataset with placeholder secrets; we provide a harness adapter that maps the scripts to Redwood runner APIs (hosted + dedicated). we also support running the scripts directly against a staging endpoint.
[02:20] Sara: are there any changes needed for streaming vs non-streaming in the harness? some of our k6 setups stream partial tokens to the client.
[02:26] Priya: streaming behavior is a bit different. for streaming we validate chunked responses and latency to first byte; the harness will need to assert partial payload times. non-streaming is easier as it's request/response. we'll provide examples for both.
[02:36] Alex: also note that streaming has different cost characteristics and sometimes different kernel paths in our runtime. we'll show a streaming vs non-streaming cost/latency comparison in the benchmark report.
[02:46] Michael: good — for dedicated capacity, are there any capacity warm-up times or cache priming steps we should include? our workloads rely on KV cache for conversation context.
[02:55] Priya: yes, we'll include a warm-up phase in the harness — prefix caching and KV cache priming. warm-up typically runs for 10-30 minutes depending on dataset size. we'll also run a cold-start run for baseline.
[03:07] Tom: can the harness measure token-level cost by route/model? we want per-route breakdowns.
[03:12] Alex: Redwood Console will provide token-level cost breakdowns per route and model. in the POC report we'll include per-route and per-model cost and latency.
[03:20] Michael: excellent. on the integration details — our security team will want to review the runner access, do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) and VPC peering for private deployments?
[03:29] Priya: yes for Private we support customer KMS/HSM integrations and VPC connectivity. for the hosted POC we use TLS + token-based auth and we can provide temporary staging creds; for anything beyond that we'll do a Private pilot.
[03:40] Sara: regarding data retention, do you persist raw requests? our audit requires minimal retention and deletion on demand.
[03:46] Alex: by default hosted runs keep logs for 30 days; we can configure retention and redact payloads. we'll include our audit log controls in the security pack.
[03:56] Michael: okay thank you. now, timeline: we were hoping for a 2-week POC with initial baseline runs in week 1 and deeper optimization in week 2. is that realistic?
[04:04] Priya: yes that's a typical tempo. week 1: integration, baseline runs against hosted + small dedicated slice, and initial report. week 2: tuning (batching, quantization recommendations) and re-run benchmarks, final report and decision.
[04:18] Tom: for dedicated we may need to provision GPUs — how long does that take?
[04:22] Alex: provision for Dedicated in our staging pool is usually 24-48 hours once the purchase order/commitments are set, but for a POC we can allocate a small reserved slice quickly; we'll confirm during kickoff.
[04:32] Michael: ok. regarding pass/fail criteria for the POC and the eval thresholds, can you run our eval suite and provide diff reports?
[04:39] Priya: yes we'll integrate your eval suite into the harness and produce diff reports with metrics like rouge, bleu, latency percentiles, and per-route token cost. we'll flag regressions per your thresholds.
[04:48] Sara: small nit — our scripts include a lot of partial-turn chat streaming; we need the harness to assert partial-response correctness, not just final text.
[04:55] Priya: we'll add streaming assertions to the adapter. if you can mark which testcases require streaming assertions that will speed things up.
[05:04] Michael: will do. question on privacy — can you run the POC on-prem if needed?
[05:08] Alex: yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem deployment but that usually requires more lead time. for the first POC we recommend hosted + dedicated to move faster, then we can evaluate Private.
[05:19] Tom: understood. another operational question — do you expose metrics endpoints (Prometheus) during the run? we want to correlate our own telemetry.
[05:25] Priya: yes we can stream metrics to a prometheus endpoint or push to a metrics sink. we'll add that to the harness config.
[05:31] Michael: good. about the harness adapter — do you take k6 scripts as-is or do you want them converted?
[05:36] Priya: we can run k6 scripts as-is if they are non-streaming; for streaming k6 needs some custom logic. often customers wrap streaming in a small node/python adapter; we'll provide an example node adapter.
[05:48] Sara: fine — we'll export our k6 and python runners.
[05:51] Alex: i'll follow up with a short runbook and example harness repo.
[05:55] Michael: excellent. now on metrics, we need: p50/p95/p99, first-byte latency for streaming, cost per 1k tokens, throughput (tokens/sec), and functional eval diffs.
[06:06] Priya: noted. any thresholds for p99?
[06:09] Michael: p99 < 800ms for chat, but it's less critical than p95; main focus is p95 and consistency across runs.
[06:17] Tom: also include error rates and fallback behavior when capacity is saturated — e.g., automatic fallback to smaller model or queued requests.
[06:23] Priya: we'll run saturation tests and validate automatic fallback policies; we'll capture error rates and tail latency during spike windows.
[06:31] Michael: do you have sample benchmark reports we can see?
[06:33] Alex: yes, i'll attach two example reports from similar customers and a template runbook.
[06:37] Sara: about cost modeling — can Redwood show us recommended quantization and batching configs to reach our cost targets?
[06:42] Priya: absolutely. Redwood Optimize will provide model/quant recommendations and expected unit economics by workload; we'll include those suggestions after baseline runs.
[06:52] Michael: great. timeline recap?
[06:55] Alex: immediate next steps: you share scripts and eval subset; we share harness adapter and security pack; kickoff integration next Tuesday (2026-03-30) and run baseline in week 1.
[07:05] Michael: agreed. one more thing — we're considering Anthropic for some of the chat flows, will you run multi-model comparisons?
[07:10] Priya: we can run comparative benchmarks against models you provide or models in our catalog. competitors like OpenAI/Anthropic/Vertex are common comparisons; note that exact model parity depends on tokenization and sampling configs, but we can normalize runs.
[07:22] Tom: okay good. any blockers from your side?
[07:25] Priya: no, just access to scripts and a staging endpoint, and confirmation of the eval subset.
[07:31] Michael: we'll share by Friday EOD.
[07:34] Alex: perfect. are we missing anything?
[07:36] Sara: maybe clarify data retention during the POC — minimal retention and deletion hooks?
[07:40] Alex: noted, we'll include retention config and a deletion flow in the security pack.
[07:44] Michael: thanks.
[07:46] Priya: ok i'll summarize action items in the follow-up email.
[07:50] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with attachments and schedule.
[07:53] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: some product names transcribed oddly (Redwood Dedicted, K-V cache spelled K V cache) in auto transcript. references: runbook link (will be shared), security pack link (will be shared), example harness repo (github.com/redwood/harness-examples).

POC Acceptance Criteria (as captured during call):
- Functional: no more than 2% degradation on eval metrics (rouge/bleu)
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for short chat responses, p95 <= 1.2s for longer streaming segments
- Throughput: aggregated batch throughput >= 10k tokens/sec for batch jobs
- Cost: cost per 1k tokens within target band provided by customer
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% during steady-state, graceful fallback during spikes

Attachments to send after call: SOC2 + security appendix, example benchmark report, harness adapter repo, pricing sheet.
